text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm about to open a terraform PR that tweaks the node pool burst window and eviction backoff for Karpenter. Need a fast sanity check before we merge. TL;DR: increase scaleDown delay, set a short eviction backoff, and update the metrics secret path used by the metrics-adapter.

jon: ping the PR link when ready. what numbers are you proposing for scaleDown + backoff? :eyes:

maya: putting it here so CI picks it up in the PR description. proposing:
```
module "karpenter" {
  eviction_backoff_seconds = 30
  scale_down_delay_seconds = 420  # 7m, was 120
  ttl_after_empty_seconds  = 300  # keep pools around a bit longer
}
```

liam: 30s eviction backoff seems fine for short bursts. 7m scale-down delay should avoid churn for training/job spikes. Have we considered namespace-level bursty HPAs?

maya: yes — we intend to add an annotation to the HPA-heavy namespaces to raise minReplicas for obvious latencies. also we will enable prefix caching on the runtime side.

ashley: question about VPA — if VPA is enabled for some services, can that trigger scale-down behavior we don't expect? VPA could evict pods during updates.

jon: VPA won't directly evict unless you have the update mode set to "Auto" and it's doing restarts. For safety, we annotate critical deployments: `vpa.kubernetes.io/update-mode: \"Off\"` and rely on manual recommendations.

jen: also +1 on PDBs to avoid mass disruptions. set `minAvailable: 1` for any singleton pods and use `maxUnavailable: 20%` for stateless pools.

maya: added that to the PR notes. another piece: metrics-adapter secret path moved in vault after the last rotate — the terraform change needs to point to `secret/data/infra/metrics-adapter/prod` instead of the old `kv/metrics/prod`. If that is missed, HPA will be on stale metrics and not scale as expected.

liam: can you include the exact terraform var name? I can grep our modules.

maya: var is `metrics_adapter_secret_path` in `modules/metrics/variables.tf`. snippet: `metrics_adapter_secret_path = \"secret/data/infra/metrics-adapter/prod\"`.

jon: quick check for Karpenter: ensure provisioner config includes `consolidation: disabled` for these pools if we want to avoid aggressive consolidation during bursts, or set consolidation delay higher.

maya: good call — added `consolidation: { enabled = true, delay_seconds = 600 }` to slow it down.

infra-bot: CI /terraform plan for branch `maya/autoscale-burst` finished — 3 changed resources, no deletions. Link: https://ci.internal/terraform/plan/12345

ashley: can we run a canary deploy on staging cluster first? run with `--target` for the provisioner and then smoke test HPAs for 15m.

maya: yes will do staging canary. plan to: 1) apply TF to staging (provisioner config + secret path) 2) scale a test HPA up with a load job 3) confirm no premature node scale-down for 10m 4) promote.

jon: for testing load, you can use this command to push CPU on a pod: `kubectl run -i --tty load --image=busybox -- /bin/sh -c \"while true; do md5sum /dev/urandom | head -c 1000000 > /dev/null; done\"`. Monitor HPA with `kubectl get hpa -w`.

liam: small ops nit: when we change TTL/scale-down timers, coordinate with oncall — we might mask signals for the autoscaler for a short window. adding `oncall` to the PR review checklist.

maya: yep will add to PR template. also will add a note to the rollout playbook about Vault secret path rotation steps.

jen: left a quick comment on the PR about the TF variable naming (suggest `metrics_adapter_vault_path` for clarity).

maya: thanks — will update.

jon: LGTM once you add the canary run instructions and update the var name.

ashley: after merge, let's schedule a 30m watch window during weekday morning to observe pod churn and node metrics.

maya: sounds good. merging only after staging smoke. thanks all! :thumbsup:
